question.prompt: A large square with side length \((a+b)\) is formed from 4 right triangles with legs \(a\) and \(b\) and hypotenuse \(c\), together with a central small square with side length \(c\). Which equation expresses the area relationship?

solutions.explanation: The area \((a+b)^2\) of the large square equals the total area \(4\times(ab/2)\) of the 4 triangles plus the area \(c^2\) of the small square. Expanding gives \(a^2+2ab+b^2=2ab+c^2\), so \(a^2+b^2=c^2\).
solutions.title: Equate the whole area and the sum of its parts
